I. C. Herried Pg 6
CONCLUSION
After a careful analysis of the environmental impact statement I have arrived at these conclusions:
4. The Highway Department has failed to justify the necessity of spending 12.1 million dollars for a project only 1.5 miles in length. Alternatives exist that are either less costly and/or more in line with the changing transportation needs and the public welfare.
B. The environmental impact statement itself is inadequate for its lack of information. To be acceptable the following data must be supplied:
1. An explanation to the fact that the Airport Spur is not included in the SENRPC, 'Proposed Land Use and Freeway System 1990'(pg 1)
2. The source of the E.P.A. quote concerning the decrease in carbon monoxide emissions. (pg 2)
3. An explanation of the inclusion of route speed when this has been ruled out as a factor. (pg 2)
4. A more accurate prediction of traffic volume anticipating the effect of a freeway facility on traffic demand. (pg 4)
5. A translation of Tons/day into lbs particulate per million (ppm's). (pg 4)
6. Adequate consideration of the College Ave. Alternative. (Pp. 5)
7. Adequate consideration of the bus lane alternative. (pg 5)
8. An origin-destination survey including ave. riders/vehicle and type of vehicle. (pg 5)
I request notification of any responses to my comments and access to any information concerning any further developments in the Airport Spur Project. I respectfully submit these comments, this 10th day of August, 1973.
I regain,
Lobbyist For Balanced Transportation
